conviction_note: The UK category data (ONS hardware/paints/glass +4.85% in Kingfisher's Q2 against +1.3% in its Q1) says the 'late spring' excuse was real and Q2 snapped back, and the disclosed short base is at or above its highest level in the whole 2016-2026 FCA record with roughly 38 sessions of median turnover to cover -- the same setup that produced +14.6% at the September 2025 H1 print on HALF this short base. Against that, the stock has already put on 6.25% in five sessions on the Wickes read-across and the Deutsche Bank upgrade, both of which are visible in the tape (+1.95/+2.42/+2.93% on 15/16/17 Sep), so most of the cyclical good news is in. My findings sum to +2.7; I emit +2.2 because the run-up has taken roughly half a point of it, and because print_vs_bar and expected_move deliberately disagree: I expect the headline to beat the published Vuma bar of GBP 372m, but that bar was last refreshed on 2 July 2026 and the marginal broker is 11% above it, so a nominal 'beat versus consensus' is worth materially less than it will read.

positioning_check: Crowded, at a decade high, and built all year. I did not take the baseline's number on trust and the two do not agree. The FCA aggregated register as I fetched it at 2026-09-21 13:52 UTC reads KINGFISHER PLC / GB0033195214 / 9.31% / position date 05/08/2026 (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv) -- the whole file's latest position date is 05/08/2026, so the FCA's published current snapshot is about six weeks stale; the baseline reports 10.69% at 16/09/2026 (prev 9.89%, +0.80pp) from a cache. I could not reproduce the 10.69%, so I treat 9.31% as the verified floor and the direction as the load-bearing part. Reconstructed from the FCA per-holder history (short-positions-daily-update.xlsx, sheet 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026'), the aggregate ran 4.28% end-Feb 2026, 6.46% end-Mar, 7.17% end-Apr, 7.51% end-May, 7.38% at 08/07/2026 -- and the all-time maximum over the file's 2016-01-27 to 2026-07-08 span is 9.22% (2022-07-26). So 9.31% already exceeds a ten-year high. Seven disclosed holders at 08/07/2026: AKO Capital 1.66, Kintbury Capital 1.37, Marshall Wace 1.29, BlackRock IM (UK) 1.14, Ilex Capital 0.82, Millennium 0.60, ExodusPoint 0.50. At 9.31% of a c.GBP 4.9bn market cap against median 20-day turnover of USD 15.96m, that is roughly 38 sessions of volume to cover. Building, not covering.

findings.finding: The UK's own official category series says Kingfisher's Q2 snapped back hard: ONS 'Retail hardware, paints & glass, value NSA, all businesses' ran +4.85% year-on-year across May-July 2026 (Kingfisher's Q2) against +1.31% across February-April (its Q1), with May alone +12.8% -- a 3.5-point sequential acceleration in exactly the weeks the company blamed for Q1's late spring, and August held at +3.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line this stock trades on. At the 23 Sep 2025 H1 print Kingfisher moved FY 25/26 adj PBT to the upper end of GBP 480-540m and lifted FCF guidance, and the shares closed +14.63% (intraday +18%). At the 25 Nov 2025 Q3 update the guide was firmed again and the shares closed +5.98%. The two events where the range was merely reiterated -- Final Results 24 Mar 2026 and the Annual Financial Report 2 Apr 2026 -- closed -2.29% and -2.01%. Source for all five dates and moves: the sealed baseline's observed_rns history off https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/KGF.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire copy and both published previews (IG 18 Sep, AskTraders 20 Sep) frame the question as unresolved -- 'can B&Q spring back to life', 'investors are looking for signs that a weak start to the year was largely down to the late arrival of spring'. If the market had read this series the question would not still be open, and the Vuma consensus would not still carry B&Q Q2 26/27 LFL at +1.3% on a bar last refreshed 2 July, before June, July and August prints existed. What everyone quotes instead is the BRC August monitor, whose aggregate non-food line was -1.2% -- which is true of non-food as a whole and is not true of this category, where August was +3.8%. Aggregate headline, specific series, opposite signs.
findings.independence: Wickes' interim results RNS of 15 September 2026 says the same thing from a direct competitor's own books: 'As anticipated, trading in Q3 so far has shown a significantly improved trend, with a step up in Retail to mid-single-digit LFL revenue growth.' https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/wickes-group--wix/wickes-group-plc-interim-results-2026/9771583

findings.finding: Kingfisher's disclosed net short is at or above its highest level in the entire ten-year FCA record and has roughly tripled since February: 4.28% end-February 2026, 7.38% at 8 July, 9.31% on the live aggregated register (position date 05/08/2026) against a 2016-2026 maximum of 9.22% set in July 2022 -- and the baseline's cached read puts it at 10.69% and still building (+0.80pp) as of 16 September. Seven disclosed sellers, c.38 sessions of median turnover to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time this stock printed a good H1 into a crowded short it squeezed violently: on 23 Sep 2025 it closed +14.63% (+18% intraday) on a disclosed short base I reconstruct at 4.64% from the same FCA file -- less than half today's. The Q3 update on 25 Nov 2025 closed +5.98% with the base around 5.5%. The two disappointments in between were small, -2.29% and -2.01%: with this much stock already sold short the down-tail on this name has been visibly shallower than the up-tail.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline's own lean pays the squeeze +3.0 and the build -1.6, netting +1.4, from a generic prior borrowed from US runs and measured nowhere in Europe. That prior cannot see the two things that make this one fat-tailed: the level is a ten-year high for THIS issuer, and the days-to-cover arithmetic (9.31% of GBP 4.9bn against USD 16m/day) is roughly 38 sessions, so an exit is not available at any speed that would let the sellers get out on the print. If the market had this in the price the stock would not be 4.8% below where it stood twenty sessions ago, and the sell-side would not sit at a 314.67p mean target barely 3% above spot with Deutsche Bank's 17 September upgrade landing at HOLD with a 300p target BELOW the current price. Nobody is positioned long for this.
findings.independence: The composition is visible from a second, independent domestic mirror: Investegate's short-positions page for KGF lists the same seven holders at the same dates (AKO 1.66% 01-Jul, Kintbury 1.37% 07-Jul, Marshall Wace 1.29% 07-Jul, BlackRock 1.14% 19-Jun, Ilex 0.82% 01-Jul, Millennium 0.6% 08-Jul, ExodusPoint 0.5% 22-Jun) -- though its stated total of 8.38% does not add up; the seven sum to 7.38%, which is what the FCA file gives. https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/KGF/short-positions

findings.finding: The bar everybody will quote tomorrow is eleven weeks old. Kingfisher's company-compiled Vuma consensus -- H1 adj PBT GBP 372m, FY GBP 580m -- carries 'Last updated 02/07/26', predating the end of the half itself, while the most recent broker move (Deutsche Bank, 17 September) sits at GBP 412m for H1, 10.8% above it, and GBP 605m for the year against a GBP 595m guidance midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the mechanism behind the two negative reactions in the baseline history: on 24 Mar 2026 (Final Results, -2.29%) and 2 Apr 2026 (-2.01%) the printed numbers were not bad, and the stock still fell, because the range was reiterated rather than firmed. A headline that clears a stale published consensus but does not move the guide has twice been sold on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced in the sense that the marginal buyer has moved -- the +6.25% five-session run-up is exactly that repricing -- and unpriced in the sense that the number the wires will anchor the headline on tomorrow morning is the stale one. If the published bar had caught up, AskTraders would not be writing on 20 September that 'a simple reiteration of existing guidance may not be enough to extend the rally', and the mean target would not still be 314.67p. This is the finding that makes print_vs_bar_pct and expected_move_pct disagree, and it is why I hold the reaction well below the beat.
findings.independence: The sell-side's own aggregate says the same: 2 strong buy, 3 buy, 11 hold, 3 sell, mean target 314.67p as of 18 September 2026, i.e. c.3% above spot, and Deutsche Bank's 17 September upgrade was to HOLD with a 300p target beneath the 305.9p sealed spot. https://www.asktraders.com/analysis/kingfisher-faces-higher-bar-into-tuesdays-interim-results

findings.finding: The record summer was bad, not good, for precisely the seasonal categories Kingfisher said B&Q is 'more exposed to': the HTA Garden Retail Monitor has UK gardening sales -5% year-on-year in June 2026 with garden furniture -7% and garden tools -9%, and -7% in August with bedding plants -11%, hardy plants -14%, plant care -14%, sundries -12% and tools -9%, as drought and hosepipe bans across half of England bit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Seasonal is the line Kingfisher itself named as the Q1 problem -- 'a late start to spring impacted footfall and seasonal demand', 'B&Q more exposed to seasonal' (Q1 26/27 trading update, 26 May 2026) -- and B&Q LFL of -4.1% that quarter was followed by a +1.71% share move, i.e. the market looked through a bad seasonal quarter once already. It is the reason the -4.1% did not cost more than it did.
findings.why_not_priced: Every English preview I read treats the record-hot summer as the bull case -- 'can B&Q spring back to life', the deferred-spring thesis -- and none of them cites the one domestic series that actually measures the category, which says the heat came with a drought that killed plants, plant care, sundries and even garden furniture. Deliberately sized small: per this stage's own rule a narrow trade panel of garden centres loses to the broad official series above, and B&Q's outdoor mix is furniture, decking, paint and BBQ rather than live plants, so this caps the seasonal snap-back rather than reversing it.
findings.independence: The same source's August update, reported independently: garden centre sales +2% including catering but -3% excluding it, with the growth coming from cafes (+10%) rather than gardening. https://www.insightdiy.co.uk/news/hta-june-garden-centre-sales-impacted-by-extreme-weather/16660.htm

findings.finding: The buyback has been switched off for eighteen days going into the print: the second GBP 50m tranche completed on 3 September 2026, taking the programme to GBP 125m of GBP 300m, and no third tranche has been announced -- there has been no 'Transaction in Own Shares' RNS since 3 September after a near-weekly cadence all year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the 23 Sep 2025 H1 print Kingfisher announced it was accelerating the then-current GBP 300m programme to complete by end-March, alongside the guidance upgrade, and the shares closed +14.63%. Capital return has been part of the positive-surprise package at this name's H1 specifically.
findings.original_quote: Kingfisher has now returned £125m of the £300m share repurchase programme
findings.why_not_priced: This is only visible by reading the RNS sequence on Investegate -- first tranche GBP 75m completed 18 June, second tranche GBP 50m announced 16 July to 'commence today and end no later than 15 September 2026' and completed 3 September, then silence. No preview mentions it. A company that has left GBP 175m of an announced programme undrawn and has stopped buying is the one most likely to announce the next tranche, or an acceleration, on results morning, and FY consensus free cash flow of GBP 473m against guidance of GBP 450-510m gives it the room. Two-sided and sized small precisely because the absence of an acceleration is the other half of the distribution.

lessons_applied: 'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' arbitrated the one contradiction in my set. The ONS category index (official, whole category, all businesses) and the HTA monitor (a trade panel of garden centres) point opposite ways; I cut the HTA finding from -0.6 to -0.4 and wrote the scoping into its own text rather than leaving two findings to half-cancel silently.

'A crowded short is fuel' plus 'understatement is the hunters' systematic error' plus 'size on the name's own reaction distribution' raised the positioning finding from +1.6 to +2.0 and its high from +5.0 to +6.0. This name did +14.63% at last September's H1 on less than half the current short base; my pre-lessons band did not contain that outcome.

'Name the line a finding lands on' moved the ONS finding from reported_quarter to guidance, because its entire value is whether the GBP 565-625m range gets narrowed up rather than reiterated, and both published previews say that is the headline number.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' forced the gap between the sum and the emission to be explicit: findings sum +2.7, emitted +2.2, and conviction_note and baseline_tension both name the run-up as what took the half point.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' checked the direction of my largest finding -- it is a squeeze call against the sellers, not a bear case agreeing with them, so it is not a restatement of the register.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' moved the CEO succession out of findings entirely into outside_window: there is no RNS scheduling an appointment for 22 September and a coin flip inside one session is worth nothing to this ranking.

'Coverage tells you which regime you are in' -- at 18 analysts the English pass did return the preview everybody has, which is why five of six emitted findings are from the local pass and the one English finding is sized at 0.3.
